question: Did Jesus forewarn the apostles of his death and resurrection?
summary: The Synoptic Gospels record Jesus making at least three explicit, detailed passion predictions to the disciples (Matt 16:21; 17:22-23; 20:18-19; Mark 8:31; 9:31; 10:33-34; Luke 9:22; 9:44; 18:31-33) — each one specifying betrayal, condemnation, death, and resurrection on the third day. John 20:9 then says, after the resurrection, "For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead." If Jesus had personally told them three times that he would rise on the third day, John 20:9 is incomprehensible.

reconcile.connective: Adam Clarke concedes the disciples' ignorance is a genuine reproach, but reads it as an undesigned mark of the Gospel's honesty rather than a fabrication.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman argues the detailed passion predictions are later, Markan vaticinia ex eventu — so the disciples' ignorance in John 20:9 reflects an earlier tradition.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It was certainly a reproach to the disciples that they had not understood this prophecy, when our Lord had given them often the most direct information concerning it. … However, this ingenuous confession of John, in a matter so dishonorable to himself, is a full proof of his sincerity, and of the truth of his narration.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke concedes the disciples' failure to grasp the resurrection despite Jesus' repeated direct forewarning was a genuine 'reproach,' then reframes that admitted tension as evidence of John's honesty — directly engaging the predictions-vs-John-20:9 gap rather than glossing over it.
excerpts.source_note_text: They knew not the scripture - Viz. Psa 16:9, Psa 16:10 : Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell - כי לא תעזב נפשי לשאול ki lo taazob naphshi l'sheol - For thou wilt not abandon my life to the grave, nor suffer thy Holy One to see corruption. It was certainly a reproach to the disciples that they had not understood this prophecy, when our Lord had given them often the most direct information concerning it. Christ had referred to the history of Jonah, Mat 12:40, which was at once the type and the proof of his own resurrection. However, this ingenuous confession of John, in a matter so dishonorable to himself, is a full proof of his sincerity, and of the truth of his narration.
